open_points.subject: 01_models.md:Model M29 — OwnerFormField
open_points.text:
Facts: the field's name; whether it belongs to the request or to its values;
how its text is read.
open_points.question: What are the complete typed fields of OwnerFormField, including any optionality or defaults?
options: Only name, a request-or-values discriminator, and a reading-kind discriminator
Those fields plus destination path, tuple position, page/action identity, or closed-list identity
A different closed set of typed facts
open_points.default_guess: Declare name: str, destination: a closed request-or-values enum, and reading_kind: a closed text/integer/boolean/enumeration enum, with no defaults.

witness.initial: A later agent must create the typed closure record and dataclass for OwnerFormField.
events: The agent translates the three prose facts into fields.
One implementation uses three scalar fields; another adds a destination path and an enumeration reference.
outcomes: The resulting model has three fields.
The resulting model has five fields and distinguishes destinations and enumeration vocabularies.
witness.observer: The generated code, contracts, and data provider consuming the model

open_points.subject: OwnerFormField destination
open_points.text: whether it belongs to the owner's request itself or to the values the owner gives
open_points.question: Is the destination fact only the binary choice request versus values, or must a row also identify the path and any tuple position within that destination?
options: Store only request versus values and infer the target member from the field name
Store an explicit destination path
Store a destination path plus tuple-position markers
open_points.default_guess: Store an explicit destination path, including positional components where required.

witness.initial: An owner action has more than one nested value or a value inside a tuple.
events: The owner submits the page field.
The interface uses the OwnerFormField row to construct the action input.
outcomes: The field name is treated as a direct member of values.
The row directs the value to a nested path or tuple position.
witness.observer: The product action receiving the constructed request

open_points.subject: OwnerFormField closed-list reading
open_points.text: as one of a closed list
open_points.question: What identifies the closed list applicable to a particular field, and is that identity a fact of OwnerFormField?
options: All such fields share one global closed list
Each row references a particular enum or vocabulary
The applicable list is inferred from the destination field's type
open_points.default_guess: Make the referenced enum or vocabulary an explicit fact of each closed-list row.

witness.initial: Two owner fields are read as closed-list values but target different enums, such as customer kind and project status.
events: The owner selects the same textual value on each page.
The interface reads both fields using their OwnerFormField rows.
outcomes: Both fields are validated against one shared list.
Each field is validated against its own referenced list.
witness.observer: The owner, who sees one submission accepted or refused differently

open_points.subject: OwnerFormField row identity and uniqueness
open_points.question: What makes two occurrences the same field, and may two rows share a field name across pages or destinations?
options: The name is globally unique and alone identifies the field
The key is page or action plus name
The complete set of row facts identifies the field and duplicate names are allowed
open_points.default_guess: Use page or product action plus field name as the field key and reject duplicate rows for that key.

witness.initial: The create-project and record-customer pages both contain a field named name.
events: The data provider constructs the owner form table.
The two pages read their submitted name fields.
outcomes: A single globally keyed name row must serve both pages.
Two page-qualified name rows may have different destinations or reading rules.
witness.observer: The owner interface and the action receiving each name

open_points.subject: OwnerFormField page and action association
open_points.text: one field of the owner's pages
open_points.question: Which owner-interface pages or product actions use this table, and how is a row associated with the page or action that reads it?
options: Every field of every owner-interface page is represented
Only fields that become inputs to selected product actions are represented
Separate per-page tables provide the association outside OwnerFormField
open_points.default_guess: Cover every submitted field that becomes a product-action input and make the owning action or form an explicit association.

witness.initial: The owner interface includes project, customer, audit, session-access, and import forms.
events: Each decides independently whether its fields must appear in the owner form table.
outcomes: One implementation consults the table for every owner action.
Another consults it only for project creation and correction.
witness.observer: The owner, whose submissions are parsed and validated through different mechanisms

open_points.subject: OwnerFormField provenance
open_points.text: The release: the owner form table the data provider holds.
open_points.question: Who creates OwnerFormField values, and from what authoritative input are they created for a release?
options: The data provider authors the rows directly
The release build derives rows from owner-page declarations
The release build derives rows from product-action request models or contracts
open_points.default_guess: The release's data provider authors and mints the rows directly from the declared owner-interface forms and action input models.

witness.initial: A request model changes a field while the owner page declaration does not.
outcomes: The manually authored row keeps the old fact.
A derived row changes with the request model.
witness.observer: The owner interface when it submits the changed action

open_points.subject: OwnerFormField model kind
open_points.text: Not persisted; a constant of the release.
open_points.question: Is OwnerFormField a runtime value dataclass instantiated by generated code, or is it structural catalog data represented with a catalog, mapping, or vocabulary kind and omitted from runtime DTO emission?
options: A runtime value model whose instances populate a release constant
A read-only catalog or mapping entry that does not become a runtime DTO
Both a runtime row model and a separately declared catalog table
open_points.default_guess: Use a runtime value row model plus a separately declared read-only catalog for the complete table.

witness.initial: The specification compiler processes Model M29.
events: One compiler interpretation treats identity value as a runtime model.
Another treats the release constant as structural catalog data.
outcomes: A dataclass OwnerFormField is emitted and instantiated by the provider.
No OwnerFormField dataclass is emitted; only provider catalog data is delivered.
witness.observer: Generated modules importing or constructing OwnerFormField
